structure_explanation.en: Two parts linked by conditional と, here 'whenever/when': passing by '通る' always triggers '思いだす' (to remember). 小学校の前 ('the front of the elementary school') is the place passed, by を because 通る treats the route as a path. 子供のころ ('childhood') is what's remembered, also by を as object of 思いだす. Target is N4 grammar; central is the conditional/temporal と of natural consequence.

Na segunda parte, 子供のころ ('a época de criança') é o que se lembra, também marcado por を como objeto de 思いだす. O foco é cobertura de gramática N4, e aqui o ponto central é o と condicional/temporal de consequência natural.

ops.issue: lit_en states a different proposition than the JP. 見えるところに目がいってしまう means 'the eyes end up going to the visible place', not 'there's more to see than the eye can take in' (abundance exceeding capacity). lit_pt mirrors the JP correctly; lit_en is a sense-changing mistranslation.

structure_explanation.en: It begins with どうしても ('no matter what / however hard one tries'), which combines with the idea of something involuntary. 見えるところに目がいって means 'one's eyes go to the visible place', with いって being the te form of 行く ('to go'); note that the tokenizer wrote the lemma as いう, but the meaning here is 行く. ops.issue: 発明者 is read はつめいしゃ (Sino-Japanese suffix 者 = しゃ), not はつめいもの. The kana teaches a wrong reading of the whole sentence.
Romaji propagates the wrong reading of 発明者 (hatsumeimono instead of hatsumeisha). Not the known punctuation/katakana issue — an actual wrong reading.

structure_explanation.en: The topic is 彼 ("he"), marked by は. The core is the target construction とされている: the particle と marks the content of the statement (その発明者, "the inventor of it"), される is the passive form of する ("to do/regard as"), and ている indicates a continuous state. Together, they form "is held/regarded as ~", "is said to be ~", expressing an attribution recognized by others, not by the speaker himself.

Juntas, formam "é tido/considerado como ~", "diz-se que é ~", expressando uma atribuição reconhecida por terceiros, não pelo próprio falante.

structure_explanation.en: The sentence uses the target pattern 〜てすみません, which apologizes for an action. The verb here is 質問攻めにする (literally 'to subject to a barrage of questions'), which appears in the te form (して) to link to the apology. The closing すみませんでした is the polite, past form of すみません ('sorry'), indicating that the apology refers to something that already happened.

O fecho すみませんでした é a forma educada e no passado de すみません ('desculpe'), indicando que o pedido de desculpas se refere a algo já ocorrido.

gloss.pt-BR: bombardeio / enxurrada (sufixo '-攻め' = atacar com algo em excesso)

role.en: noun (part of the compound, head of 質問攻め)
role.pt-BR: substantivo (parte do composto, núcleo de 質問攻め)

gloss.en: to make / to turn (someone into a target of something)

note.en: て form of する (して); connects to すみません
note.pt-BR: forma-て de する (して); conecta-se a すみません

gloss.en: to be excusable (root of すみません)
gloss.pt-BR: estar/ser desculpável (raiz de すみません)

note.en: stem of すむ used in すみません(でした)
note.pt-BR: raiz de すむ usada em すみません(でした)

note.en: irrealis form of ます (ませ), required by the negation ん
note.pt-BR: forma irreal de ます (ませ), exigida pela negação ん

note.en: ん = negative ぬ; ませ+ん = ません ('not')
note.pt-BR: ん = negativo ぬ; ませ+ん = ません ('não')

note.en: でし form of です, base of the past でした
note.pt-BR: forma でし de です, base do passado でした

note.en: た = past; でし+た = でした
note.pt-BR: た = passado; でし+た = でした
